gloss: A thin soft tube left in the wound for a few days to draw off blood and saliva. An instrument, not anatomy.
role: Many surgeons leave a thin soft tube, a drain, in the wound for a day or more to draw off blood and saliva. In one hospital's routine it comes out through a separate small cut in the neck, away from the nerve.
matters: The drain lies in the space left by the gland and leaves through a stab incision in the neck so that it does not rest directly on the facial nerve.
